For starters: the best relationship I have had is clearly the one I have with my wife. In terms of worst relationships. It's honestly a tie between all of the previous ones. But I've moved on from them. Let's just say that there is some pretty hardcore suckage involved when someone who knows you intimately somehow becomes an enemy. There's an adage, "hurt people hurt people" -- and that's exactly what it's like. You are hurt, the other person is hurt, and all you want to do is hurt the other person more. And because you know the person so well, your stockpile of ammunition is excessive. It might sound deterring, but if the gamble pays off (which it eventually did for me), the risk is worth it.

All of my relationships have ended with the same lesson:

You can't expect someone to love you more than you love yourself.

Six relationships later, I finally got it. You aren't in a relationship to find happiness; you should be able to be happy without them. If you can't love and perfect the most important person in your life, then you probably don't have the best judgement as to what love is in the first place.

Between such episodes, the sufferer goes on as normal with healthy eating and exercise, thus not usually gaining weight.
The difference between this and bulimia is that they don't use throwing up, exercise, fasting, restricting, or laxatives to compensate for said binges.
